audit_notes: Model: uniform shear through the fibre-reinforced layer, u'' = 0, u(0)=0 at the primer, surface strain du/dxi(1) = tau*L/G_eff with G_eff = E_m/3 + 3*V_f*E_f*r^2/L^2 (matrix shear modulus plus the shear stiffness of guided-cantilever fibres spanning the layer). Areal compliance C = u(1)/tau, release stress sigma_c = sqrt(2w/C). Design: G_eff = 3.33e4 + 3*0.05*3e9*(5e-6/3e-4)^2 = 3.33e4 + 1.25e5 = 1.58e5 Pa; C = 3e-4/1.58e5 = 1.9e-9 m/Pa; sigma_c = 7.3 kPa. Baseline: uniform commercial topcoat E = 1 MPa, 150 um, no fibres: C = 4.5e-10 m/Pa, sigma_c = 14.9 kPa. Expected gain ~51 %. Compressive modulus of the design ~V_f*E_f = 150 MPa (vs ~3 MPa bulk modulus-limited indentation stiffness of a thin soft layer is actually confinement-dominated; the gain in indentation resistance is real for loads spread over areas larger than the layer thickness). Structural check: Euler buckling of clamped-clamped fibres sigma_cr = pi^2*E_f*r^2/L^2 = 8.2 MPa per fibre, 0.41 MPa as composite stress without matrix support; the soft matrix adds lateral support, but fender pressures of ~1 MPa will buckle fibres elastically (recoverable for nylon), so the indentation benefit saturates. Fibre-matrix interfacial shear under a 10 kPa base load is small (shear strain 0.063). Caveats: (1) fibres must be fully covered by a ~20-50 um soft skin, otherwise tips create roughness and fouling anchor points; (2) the guided-cantilever assumption requires good fibre bonding at the primer and at the skin; (3) the gradient of fibre density described in the concept is not modelled (uniform fibres); (4) release under peel rather than shear is governed by the much higher normal stiffness and would be harder. Dimensionless: slenderness L/r = 60, fibre-to-matrix shear contribution ratio 3.75, shear strain at 10 kPa 0.063. Simulation coefficient: effective shear modulus 1.58e5 Pa (informational).
